correctness.rationale: For Y=Sigma_rho^{-1}xi and a=(1-rho^2)^(-1), b=-rho*a, Wick fourth moments give the displayed 3x3 degree-two density-derivative Hermite Gram. D*=diag(1,sqrt(2),1) gives exact eigenvectors (1,±sqrt(2),1)/2 and (1,0,-1)/sqrt(2), eigenvalues 2/(1+rho)^2, 2/(1-rho)^2, 2/(1-rho^2). Since the two extreme eigenvectors have identical coordinatewise squares, every positive diagonal alternative T has equal denominators ||T^(-1)v_ext||^2, forcing kappa(TBG T)>=kappa(B); equality forces T scalar because both extreme eigenvectors have no zero entries. At rho=0 B=2I makes uniqueness immediate. Jacobi-normalized even-block eigenvalue product and odd eigenvalue show the sharp ratio 9/8 as |rho| rises to 1. Independently evaluated representative spectra at rho=-.9,-.4,0,.25,.72; samples are corroboration and the global proof is the Rayleigh argument.
